answer: Each epoch a node first seals a state root over its dedicated 4GB RAM array, committing a unique Blake3 hash of the raw bytes; the verifier then demands that same node replay the array at the next dawn, re-deriving the hash byte-for-byte. A fake identity cannot clone this garden of committed memory without buying its own 4GB and re-seeding, so forging one plume of valid history costs roughly $0.40 of RAM-hours per epoch and compounds across every sockpuppet. On mismatch the root is rejected, stake slashed, identity ejected.
